jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor - Stratigraphy and Subsurface Geology
jobs.description:
The School of Natural Resources at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (UNL) Institute of Agriculture and Natural Resources (IANR) is seeking applications for an assistant or associate stratigraphy and subsurface geology professor position. This position is housed in the Conservation and Survey Division (CSD), which serves as Nebraska’s geological survey.
  
  
Located in Lincoln, Nebraska, this 12-month (calendar year), tenure-track appointment will advance understanding of the regional geology of Nebraska and the Midcontinent, with emphasis on bedrock and deeper, older geologic units, and will apply that knowledge to groundwater, mineral, and energy resources. The apportionment is 75% research and 25% teaching.
  
  
**Research – 75%**

As appropriate to the appointment, the incumbent will build a nationally recognized, externally funded research program in stratigraphy and subsurface geology, focused on the bedrock and deeper subsurface of Nebraska and the Midcontinent and applications relevant to water and geologic resources.
  
  
The faculty member will provide scientific leadership toward a modern, three-dimensional understanding of the state’s subsurface geology. They will work in collaborative research teams and complement existing strengths of the School of Natural Resources, Conservation and Survey Division, Biological Systems Engineering, Civil and Environmental Engineering, and the Daugherty Water for Food Global Institute. They will draw on CSD’s extensive subsurface collections and recent investments in geophysical equipment by CSD, as well as newer geophysical data in Nebraska and the surrounding region. They will also apply that understanding to groundwater, mineral, and energy resources, including hydrostratigraphy, critical minerals, and geological hydrogen.
  
  
Scholarly products will include peer-reviewed publications, as well as geologic maps and data that serve state agencies, Natural Resources Districts, industry, and the public. The position will complement existing strengths in the School of Natural Resources and CSD in geologic mapping, hydrogeology, geophysics, water science, and cyberinfrastructure. The incumbent is expected to collaborate across the university and with state and federal partners.

**Teaching – 25%**
  
The incumbent will be expected to average 0.25 FTE as determined by the CASNR Teaching and Learning Expectations. Responsibilities will include developing a lower-level course with focus on earth materials and human influences to be taught annually and one additional undergraduate or graduate course in the successful candidate’s area of expertise, along with advising graduate students and mentoring undergraduates.
  
  
In addition to the above-described duties, the individual will be expected to accept committee assignments, reporting responsibilities, and other special ad hoc assignments as requested at the administrative unit, college/division, institute, and/or university level.
  
  
**About Us**

To learn about UNL benefits and your total compensation, please see: **https://go.unl.edu/aboutus**. Learn more about Lincoln, NE at **About Lincoln | Nebraska**.

  

Recognizing that collaboration and participation in teams enhances creativity, innovation, impact, and a sense of belonging, the Institute of Agriculture and Natural Resources (IANR) and the School of Natural Resources are committed to creating learning, research, and Extension programming environments where the unique contributions of each individual are acknowledged and valued. At IANR we see every person and every interaction as important to our collective wellbeing and our ability to deliver on our mission.

Minimum Required Qualifications

* Ph.D. in geology, geoscience, or Earth science at the time of appointment.
* Research expertise in stratigraphy, sedimentary geology, and the application of those fields to resource issues.
* A record of peer-reviewed publications appropriate to career stage.
* Evidence of the ability to build a nationally recognized, externally funded research program.
* For appointment at the rank of Associate Professor, a record of scholarship, extramural funding, and teaching that meets UNL’s criteria for appointment at that rank.

Preferred Qualifications

* A record of competitive extramural funding.
* Experience integrating stratigraphic observations with geophysical, geochemical, or geospatial data to develop geologic maps or three-dimensional subsurface models.
* Research experience applying stratigraphy to groundwater, mineral, or energy resources, such as hydrostratigraphy, critical minerals, or geological hydrogen.
* Experience relevant to the regional geology of Nebraska, the Great Plains, or the interior of North America.
* Successful experience teaching and mentoring undergraduate and graduate students, and communicating science to agencies, industry, and the public.

* A letter of interest that describes your qualifications for the job and anticipated contributions.

* Your curriculum vitae.

-------------------------

The School of Information Studies (SIS) in the College of Human Sciences & Education (CHSE) at Louisiana State University (LSU) invites applications for a tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor in Computational Archival Science, to start in August 2027.

**Tenure-Track Position: Assistant Professor**

Computational Archival Science (CAS) is an emerging interdisciplinary field that incorporates computational methods into the creation, management, preservation, and use of records and archives. It also brings archival principles such as provenance, authenticity, integrity, and evidentiary value to data, algorithms, and AI systems. We seek a colleague who works in both directions and who will help build LSU's research strength in trustworthy digital information.

SIS invites candidates with demonstrated potential for research and teaching in one or more of the following areas:

* Machine learning, NLP, and generative AI for archival functions such as appraisal, arrangement and description, metadata creation, and access
* Born-digital, government, and large-scale records, including email, web, and social media archives
* Data integrity, authenticity, and provenance of digital records, including trustworthy and secure recordkeeping infrastructures
* Digital preservation, digital forensics, and long-term information infrastructure
* Sensitivity review, privacy, and redaction in records and archives
* AI governance and recordkeeping, including AI systems and their outputs as records
* Collections as data, linked data, knowledge graphs, and computational access to archives
* Human-centered, ethical, and community-centered approaches to automated systems in archives and memory institutions

This is a nine-month position. The teaching load is two courses per semester. Summer research funding and summer teaching may also be available. Salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.

**Responsibilities:** **The faculty member will build a funded research program in Computational Archival Science, teach across archival and computational topics, and complete professional- and university-related service.**
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

* **Research:** Conduct scholarly research in Computational Archival Science that leads to publication in peer-reviewed journals and conferences. Seek external funding from agencies such as NSF, IMLS, NEH, and defense- and security-related sponsors. Build interdisciplinary partnerships across LSU and with archives, libraries, government agencies, and industry.
* **Teaching:** Teach and develop courses in the MLIS program, graduate certificates, and the undergraduate Digital Studies minor. Topics may include archives and records management, digital curation and preservation, and computational and AI methods for information professionals. Contribute to the School's planned growth in undergraduate and graduate programs.
* **Service:** Participate actively in service that advances the mission of the School, the College, and the University, and engage with professional communities.
* **Other Duties Assigned**

**Minimum Qualifications:**
---------------------------

* Ph.D. in Information Science or an allied field by the time of appointment. Allied fields include, but are not limited to, Archival Studies, Library and Information Science, Computer Science, Data Science, Digital Humanities, and Information Systems. Research focus in Computational Archival Science or a closely related area, applying computational methods to records and archives or archival principles to data and AI systems. Demonstrated potential for excellence in research and publication. Ability to teach graduate courses that connect archival concepts with computational methods.

**Preferred Qualifications:**
-----------------------------

* A research agenda that advances LSU's Defense & Cyber priority, for example, data integrity, authenticity, provenance, secure recordkeeping, or the preservation of government and security-relevant records. Research on human-centered or responsible AI in archives, records, or memory institutions, aligned with CHSE's Human-Centered AI, Information & the Future of Learning and Work area. Evidence of a robust research agenda through a publication record and success, or clear potential for success, in obtaining external research funding. Hands-on technical expertise, such as machine learning, NLP, digital forensics, or scalable data pipelines, paired with grounding in archival theory and practice. Experience in interdisciplinary research and in partnerships with archives, libraries, museums, government agencies, or industry. Experience teaching in-person and/or online asynchronous courses, and the ability to teach both archival and computational courses.

**Strategic Fit: LSU and CHSE Priorities:**
-------------------------------------------

This position advances LSU's research priorities and CHSE's strategic direction. The successful candidate will be expected to build these priorities through research, teaching, and partnerships.

**LSU's Defense & Cyber Priority.**

LSU invests in five research areas to meet Louisiana's greatest needs: Agriculture, Biotechnology, Coast & Environment, Defense & Cyber, and Energy. Trustworthy records are a foundation of national security and cybersecurity. This position contributes to Defense & Cyber through research on data integrity, authenticity, and provenance of digital records, secure and resilient information infrastructure, and the long-term preservation of government and institutional records. It also supports LSU's broader AI and data agenda.

**CHSE's Human-Centered AI, Information & the Future of Learning and Work.**

The position anchors this strategic area in SIS, the fastest-growing school in the College by enrollment. We welcome research that keeps people, communities, and institutional missions at the center of automated systems. Examples include evaluating AI tools for archival work, governing AI systems and their outputs as records, and preparing information professionals for AI-enabled work.

We especially welcome candidates whose work connects to LSU's other priority areas through records and data. Examples include environmental and coastal records, agricultural and rural community archives, health records, and energy-sector information.

**About the LSU School of Information Studies:**
------------------------------------------------

The LSU School of Information Studies (SIS), a member of the iSchools consortium, is a dynamic and growing school within the College of Human Sciences & Education. For over 90 years, SIS has been at the forefront of information studies. Today it is a research-intensive school with a strong commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration and to addressing complex challenges. Our faculty hold over $2 million in active research grants from agencies including the Institute of Museum and Library Services (IMLS), the National Science Foundation (NSF), and the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

SIS is home to over 1,500 graduate students in our nationally recognized, ALA-accredited Master of Library and Information Science (MLIS) program. SIS also offers graduate certificates and an undergraduate minor in Digital Studies. Our strategic vision is to expand our research and academic programs, including new undergraduate and doctoral programs, and to grow our faculty in key areas such as data science, artificial intelligence, computational archival science, and health information.

For more information, visit the School of Information Studies.

The University of Virginia’s Center for Teaching Excellence (CTE; https://cte.virginia.edu/ ) seeks applicants for an Assistant Director or Associate Director (AD), depending on qualification. The position is ideal for passionate educational developers excited to expand CTE’s capacity in areas aligned with institutional priorities such as STEM education, generative AI, graduate student professional development and/or experiential education.

Reporting to the CTE Executive Director, the AD will serve as a academic general faculty member (not tenure eligible), supporting instructors and academic units through consultations, resource and program development, program assessment, cross-school partnerships, and organizational development initiatives. The position’s cross-disciplinary focus creates opportunities to strengthen collaboration with schools and units pursuing related priorities, particularly in AI and STEM education. This will require the AD to…

* support instructors and academic units through consultations, program development, and assessment
* build and sustain cross-school partnerships and contribute to university-level conversations and initiatives in STEM education, AI in teaching and learning, graduate student education, and/or experiential education.
* expand the CTE’s scholarship and assessment work in areas of mutual interest.
* teach annually in their disciplinary area of expertise, in keeping with the CTE’s teaching mission.

The CTE, which is a nationally recognized, mature, well-resourced, and growing center for teaching and learning, especially seeks experienced educational developers who embrace the center’s mission and core values of educational equity and inclusion, who thrive in work settings that encourage autonomy, creativity, and teamwork, and who wish to engage deeply in meaningful work in a supportive environment. The AD will leverage their established knowledge and expertise in inclusive pedagogies to advance CTE work (~70% of effort), engage in scholarly activity (~15% of effort), and teach one undergraduate course per year (~15% of effort). The AD is expected to work in person and may choose to adopt a hybrid work model that includes a mix of in-office and remote work, with a minimum of two in-office work days each week.

As a member of UVA’s non-tenure track, general faculty, the AD is eligible for 1) promotion through the professorial ranks, 2) sabbaticals, and 3) consulting opportunities. Initial rank—assistant or associate professor—will depend on the selected candidate’s qualifications and experience.

  

Candidates must possess these minimum qualifications:

* Terminal degree in any field
* Minimum of 3 years of work in educational development, instructional development, or closely related role in higher education.
* Experience designing, implementing, and leading instructional development programming at the school or university level, including communities of practice, faculty learning communities, or multi-day institutes.
* Demonstrated ability to collaborate with faculty, graduate students, academic units, and schools across disciplines.

* Strong written and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to build and maintain collaborative partnerships.
* Ability to work independently and as a part of a collaborative team.

Though not required to be competitive, the CTE especially encourages candidates to apply with qualifications or experience in any of the following areas:

* Experience supporting STEM faculty, graduate student professional development, generative AI, and /or experiential learning.
* Research or scholarship in STEM education, graduate student professional development, generative AI and/or experiential learning.

This is a renewable General Faculty appointment, with renewal contingent upon satisfactory performance and continued need for the position.

For additional information about the position, please contact Lindsay Wheeler, Acting CTE Director, at lsb4u@virginia.edu.

This position will remain open until filled. Anticipated Hiring Range: $75,000 - $95,000 commensurate with education and experience.

**Position Announcement**
-------------------------

The Department of Social and Behavioral Sciences in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences at Utah Valley University invites applications for tenure-track faculty positions in Social Work at the assistant, associate, or full professor rank. Appointments will begin in August 2027.
  
  
These positions provide an exciting opportunity to contribute to the continued growth and development of UVU’s Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) and Master of Social Work (MSW) programs. Both programs are fully accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE).
  
  
UVU’s social work programs provide effective instruction and mentorship to students with varied educational backgrounds and life experiences; maintain a respectful, professional, and student-centered learning environment; use teaching practices and course materials appropriate to the course learning outcomes and applicable accreditation standards; and work professionally with students, colleagues, and community partners.
  
  
The successful candidate will collaborate with social work faculty in developing and establishing curriculum, activities, processes, resources, and policies that support student development of social work knowledge, skills, and values. The appointee’s workload expectations will be teaching (80%), research (10%), and institutional service (10%). The position carries a teaching load of 24 credit hours or equivalent per academic year, typically 12 credits per semester (4/4).
  
  
UVU offers extensive resources and professional-development workshops to support and enhance teaching effectiveness. The successful candidate will use pedagogical approaches that promote student engagement, establish measurable course learning objectives, and assess student learning through written assignments, oral and/or skills-based assessments, examinations, and other appropriate evaluation methods.
  
  
The successful candidate will collaborate professionally with faculty and staff to support the well-being and continued development of the social work programs, the Department of Social and Behavioral Sciences, the College of Humanities and Social Sciences, Utah Valley University, and its students and employees. A commitment to collegiality, collaboration, and student success is essential
  
  
The successful candidate is expected to uphold the professional mission, purpose, and ethics of the social work profession and comply with applicable university policies and legal requirements.

**Summary of Responsibilities**
-------------------------------

* Teaching courses in the Social Work Discipline.

Prepares all instructional materials (to include course syllabi, exams, readings, instructions, visual aids, and other materials) in electronic and paper formats. **Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience working effectively with under-resourced populations.

**JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY**

WPI’s Department of Integrative and Global Studies seeks a full-time, tenure track Assistant Professor of Teaching, whose teaching, advising, and scholarly expertise will support WPI’s undergraduate interdisciplinary projects program.

**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**About WPI**

Worcester Polytechnic Institute was founded in 1865 to create and convey the latest science and engineering knowledge in ways that are most beneficial to society. Today, WPI holds firm to its founding mission to provide an education that balances theory with practice. WPI's 14 academic departments offer more than 50 undergraduate and graduate degree programs in science, engineering, technology, business, the social sciences, and the humanities and arts, leading to bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral degrees.

The university’s curriculum features a rigorous but flexible program that is project-based and globally-engaged, aimed at quality experience and positive engagement with communities around the world. WPI faculty members work with students on interdisciplinary research and design, addressing important and socially relevant challenges, both on campus and at more than 50 project centers throughout the Americas, Africa, Asia-Pacific, and Europe.

  

**About the Department of Integrative and Global Studies**

WPI’s Department of Integrative and Global Studies (DIGS) serves as a gateway for students and faculty to connect with and make a difference in communities around the world. The department is the intellectual home of experiential and community-based learning at the university, providing stewardship for the university’s signature Global Projects Program . The Global Projects Program is an interdisciplinary, project-based learning initiative that engages students in collaborative, community-centered research and problem-solving with local and international partners to address real-world challenges. It offers a distinctive, interdisciplinary project experience that challenges students to address problems at the intersection of science, technology and society.

  

WPI requires students to work in teams to complete a nine-credit hour project that confronts an open-ended problem at the interface of society and technology, and most students fulfill this requirement through an 8-week term at one of the project centers around the world. DIGS faculty members advise students through the full arc of these team-based projects. They teach a preparation course on research methods and design thinking; they travel with students and supervise projects at one of the university’s 50+ global project centers; and they help student process these experiences to advance career readiness and lifelong learning. In most cases, faculty co-advise these projects with other faculty members. The faculty also build on relationships at these global project centers to conduct research on topics such as sustainable food systems, urban planning, innovation and entrepreneurship, conservation, climate resilience, community development, and many other topics, including pedagogical research around project-based and community-engaged learning.

  

DIGS faculty also deliver the first-year project-based learning program, the Great Problems Seminar, which guides students through team-based projects addressing global grand challenges as part of a campus-based course.

  

**About the Position**

WPI’s Department of Integrative and Global Studies seeks a full-time, tenure track Assistant Professor of Teaching, whose teaching, advising, and scholarly expertise will support WPI’s undergraduate interdisciplinary projects program.

  

**Principal Duties and Responsibilities**

* Successful candidates will prepare students for a nine-credit, team-based off-campus research project and design experience by teaching Social Science Research Methods and advising student projects at WPI’s off campus project centers for one or two 8-week terms per year.

* Faculty responsibilities include classroom teaching, organizing and advising student research and design projects, and advancing high impact, innovative approaches to teaching and learning.

* Over time, the successful candidate will be expected to take a leadership role in directing one of the off-campus project centers that comprise WPI’s domestic and global project network.

* Successful candidates for this tenure track Assistant Professor of Teaching role are expected to be excellent teachers and project advisors, and active pedagogical innovators who develop and disseminate high impact teaching practices.

Faculty are also expected to participate in pre-departure training and orientation activities to ensure students are prepared to address health and safety issues while traveling , as well as department meetings and departmental service activities.  



**Desired Attributes**

* Experience teaching qualitative social science research methods and conducting applied field research or community engagement.

* Experience engaging students in off-campus experiential learning in diverse communities and organizational settings.

* Demonstrated ability to collaborate with colleagues from a variety of disciplines.

* Demonstrated evidence of flexibility, adaptability, and ability to pivot while guiding students.

* Creativity in approaches to applied social science methods and collaborative design.

* Strong interest in global engagement and experience engaging a wide variety of audiences including undergraduates, field professionals, scholars, policymakers, and other community stakeholders.

* Experience with creative pedagogical approaches in the classroom.

* Active engagement in workshops, conferences, and other professional communities.

* Experience in relevant integrative settings, such as but not limited to, international field schools, experiential or project-based learning, cross-cultural engagement, non-profit management, foreign service, or corporate or public sector decision-making.

Demonstrated global and intercultural competency, such as through language or other cross cultural engagement skills.  

  

**Position Requirements**

A PhD in a relevant integrative field, such as but not limited to, Anthropology, Geography, History, International Studies or Development, Psychology, Sociology, Education, Environmental and Sustainability Studies, Human-Centered Design, or Communication.  

  

**How to Apply**

For full consideration, applications, including a cover letter (2 page max), CV, teaching statement (2 page max), research statement (2 page max), and contact information for references should be received by December 10, 2026.

  

Please note that we are also hiring a secure contract teaching faculty position in DIGS. Qualified applicants are welcome to submit applications for both positions.

  

**Compensation**

Salary: $82,500 - $85,000 per year. Salary is based on related experience, expertise, and internal equity. WPI’s benefits package includes a robust retirement match, wellness perks, tuition assistance and more!

**FLSA STATUS**

United States of America (Exempt)

**WPI is an Equal** **Opportunity Employer. All qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, age, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or disability. It seeks individuals from all backgrounds and experiences who will contribute to a culture of creativity, collaboration, inclusion, problem solving, innovation, high performance, and change making. It is committed to maintaining a campus environment free of harassment and discrimination.**
